title: Personal Loans Late Fee Terms: Grace Period, State Schedules and Exclusions
content:
## Terms in force

A late fee is charged on a Personal Loans installment that is still not paid in full when its grace period ends. The late fee may be assessed only when the current date is later than the installment due date plus the late-fee grace period. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the installment due date, so with a 15-day grace period an installment due on the 1st can first be charged a late fee on the 17th. At most one late fee is charged for one installment. Late fees are assessed only on a loan in active status.

The amount depends on the state fee schedule fixed by the loan's origination state, applied to the unpaid portion of that installment on the assessment date - the scheduled installment amount or the amount past due, whichever is smaller:

| Origination state | Fee schedule |
|---|---|
| CA, CO, CT, MA, ME, MN, NY, VT | B |
| MD, NC, WI | C |
| every other state where Larkspur lends | A |

No schedule ever charges more than the unpaid portion itself. No late fee is charged when the installment is short only because part of an on-time, full payment was applied to an earlier late fee or returned-payment fee (late fees are never pyramided). No late fee is charged for an installment whose due date falls inside an active hardship plan on the loan, for an installment deferred by a hardship plan, or while a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit is active on the loan. A borrower's move to another state does not change the schedule.

## Clause no longer in force

The clause below is no longer in force for a late fee assessed under the current Personal Loans late-fee figuring, which works the fee out from the schedule figure:

> Schedule A charges the schedule A late-fee percent of the unpaid portion but not less than the schedule A minimum and not more than the schedule A maximum; schedule B charges the schedule B percent of the unpaid portion but not more than the schedule B maximum; schedule C charges the schedule C flat fee.

Otherwise schedule A charges its percent of the unpaid portion but not less than its minimum and not more than its maximum, schedule B its percent of the unpaid portion but not more than its maximum, and schedule C its flat fee.

## Grace boundary (15-day grace period, hypothetical due dates)

| Installment due | Day 15 of the grace period | First day a late fee may be assessed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 May | 16 May | 17 May |
| 20 June | 5 July | 6 July |

On 16 May an installment due 1 May cannot yet be charged; on 17 May it can, if still unpaid.

superseded_clauses: schedule_a charges late_fee_schedule_a_percent of the unpaid portion but not less than late_fee_schedule_a_min_usd and not more than late_fee_schedule_a_max_usd; schedule_b charges late_fee_schedule_b_percent of the unpaid portion but not more than late_fee_schedule_b_max_usd; schedule_c charges late_fee_schedule_c_flat_usd.
